brief.data: Fleet: 22 ATR 72-600 aircraft with tail numbers, manufacturer serial numbers and embodied service bulletins. The manual library holds about 4,800 task cards organized by ATA chapter (e.g., 32-42 Brakes), each with card number, title, revision number and date, effectivity range by serial number, estimated labor hours, required tools and parts, and status (current, superseded, temporary revision active). 3 temporary revisions issued in the last 14 days, including TR 32-018 changing brake retaining bolt torque from 45 to 50 Nm. Recently opened cards are shown per aircraft. Open work order WO-88213 is for N614RG: brake wear pin at limit, left main gear, position 2.

prompt:
I need the front end for TaskCard Station. A shared maintenance-manual reference terminal mounted in the hangars of a regional airline's maintenance base, where technicians look up the approved task cards and manual sections for the aircraft in front of them.

Who's using it: Two night-shift aircraft maintenance technicians at the airline's Duluth base: Sam Ortega, a lead with 18 years on turboprops, and Bethany Lowe, a newly certified A&P mechanic six months into the job. Both are in gloves and standing at the terminal on the hangar floor, a few steps from the aircraft. Other techs walk up to use it during the shift.

What they're doing right now: ATR 72-600 tail N614RG came in with a worn left main gear brake flagged on the inbound logbook. It has to be fixed and signed off before its 06:10 departure. Sam and Bethany need to narrow thousands of task cards down to the right brake assembly removal and installation procedure for this specific aircraft serial number. This aircraft has a modified brake part number from a recent service bulletin, so two versions of the card apply to different serials. A temporary revision was issued last week that changes a torque value. They need to confirm they have the current, effective version and pull up the related wheel removal card. Then they have to hand the terminal over to another tech waiting on a different aircraft.

What's in the system at this point: Fleet: 22 ATR 72-600 aircraft with tail numbers, manufacturer serial numbers and embodied service bulletins. The manual library holds about 4,800 task cards organized by ATA chapter (e.g., 32-42 Brakes), each with card number, title, revision number and date, effectivity range by serial number, estimated labor hours, required tools and parts, and status (current, superseded, temporary revision active). 3 temporary revisions issued in the last 14 days, including TR 32-018 changing brake retaining bolt torque from 45 to 50 Nm. Recently opened cards are shown per aircraft. Open work order WO-88213 is for N614RG: brake wear pin at limit, left main gear, position 2.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
